findings.title: SQL disable is a dead flag check that always returns false
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions reads FlagSqlExpressions, inverts it, and then returns false from both branches. SQL expressions are therefore always rejected, but the check does not implement a real allow/deny policy and looks like a mistaken edit. A later cleanup that “fixes” the inversion (return the flag, or return true when the flag is on) would re-open the DuckDB SQL expression path that this change is meant to kill for CVE-2024-9264. The disable should be an obvious unconditional false (or the SQL command type removed), not a flag read whose result is discarded.

findings.title: Rejection error says SQL expressions are unimplemented
findings.body: When a SQL expression is parsed, ReadQuery returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). That text is wrong: the type was implemented and is being hard-disabled because DuckDB evaluation allowed RCE/LFI. Operators and the still-documented feature flag will treat this as a missing feature to turn back on, not as an intentional security shutdown. The error should say SQL expressions are disabled.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions cannot run
findings.body: The security fix only stubs sql.DB and adds a gate in ExpressionQueryReader. UnmarshalSQLCommand still builds a SQLCommand and Execute still calls QueryFramesInto; both fail only because the new stubs return "not implemented". Nothing in this change asserts that a SQL expression query is rejected on the reader path and on UnmarshalSQLCommand/Execute, or that no DuckDB/process call is made. A partial revert that restores a real TablesList or QueryFramesInto would ship without a failing test.
